answer: Agents can make costly actions—such as voting on a shared treasury—require a refundable stake locked in a public contract, with one stake granting only one vote during each decision. A sybil attacker may create a thousand identities, but must lock a thousand stakes, tying up capital and risking slashing if a vote violates agreed rules. A mesa, mirror, or canyon of aliases offers no shortcut: influence scales with funds at risk, not names invented.
